key_insight: VIME uses classical imaginary-time pre-training of a compressed Majorana-inspired ansatz to prepare molecular ground states with much lower quantum circuit cost.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce CNOT count and two-qubit depth for early fault-tolerant chemistry workloads, making hardware-efficient state preparation more practical.
method: Extend OVQITE to molecular electronic structure via a single compiled Majorana-propagation surrogate graph
Pre-train a compressed tiled Unitary Product State (c-tUPS) ansatz classically
Use the trained ansatz as a low-cost starting point for quantum ground-state preparation
evidence_signal: Across TLD-1411 and acene benchmarks up to 60 qubits, the method reached chemical accuracy or better while using up to 26× fewer CNOTs and 167× lower two-qubit depth than ADAPT-VMPE comparison points.
watch_item: The approach depends on effective classical pre-training and surrogate compilation, so performance may vary with system size, active-space choice, and ansatz expressibility.
paper_title: Hardware-Efficient Ground-State Preparation using Variational Imaginary-Time Majorana Evolution
